purpose: Define explicit merge/reconciliation of competing or migrated canonical artifacts without guessing semantic precedence or silently combining conflicting ownership.

topics.name: Reconciliation Merge
topics.purpose: Define explicit merge/reconciliation of competing or migrated canonical artifacts without guessing semantic precedence or silently combining conflicting ownership.

semantics.merge_rule: Merge is identity- and ownership-aware rather than text/line-based only.
semantics.same_identity_rule: Artifacts claiming the same canonical identity are compared semantically before reconciliation.
semantics.conflict_rule: Conflicting semantic ownership or machine-significant values remain explicit conflicts until resolved by an authorized reconciliation decision.
semantics.topic_rule: Non-conflicting Topic memberships may be unioned where the Topic model allows multi-membership.
semantics.reference_rule: References are resolved/rewritten only to exact canonical identities.
semantics.history_rule: Superseded source artifacts remain traceable through reconciliation provenance.

invariants.rule: Reading, writing, normalization, diffing, reconciliation and patching preserve canonical identity, ownership, Topic context and machine-significant semantics.

hard_gates.condition: merge resolves semantic conflict by file timestamp/path heuristic

Topic memberships unnecessarily collapsed to one

references.purpose: Reconciliation uses semantic differences rather than raw file differences.
